- **Story:** As the product owner, I want to know how often a planted defect in AI-written code survives Phrase's generated specs compared with the tests a model writes for plain C#, so that I can see whether Phrase makes AI-written code verifiable.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a design Decider written before any row, When it is read, Then it fixes the tasks, the frozen mutant operators (those of card 106 plus any added before the first row), the models that write the implementations and the C# tests, the proof levels, N, the success sentence and the Goodhart guard, and a check fails if it is missing or dated after the first row
  2. Given AI-written implementations of the same tasks in both forms, When the planted mutants are run against each form's checks, Then each row records the arm, task, mutant operator, built or not, and killed or survived, and the survivors are listed by operator
  3. Given the rows, When summarized, Then the undetected-defect rate per arm and operator is shown with its uncertainty and no verdict beyond the pre-registered sentence, beside the published head-to-head benchmark

## Context

- Goodhart guard (D99): the design Decider fixes before any row the sample, the planted cases or mutants, the scoring rubric, timing and blinding or randomization, the model and reviewer versions and matched proof levels; mutant operators and review cases are frozen and sealed from the authors who tune Phrase; speed is reported with accuracy; the success sentence is written first.
